after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{-5{x}^{7}+1}{10{x}^{3}+x+3}.$
after.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{3}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{-5{x}^{7}+1}{10{x}^{3}+x+3} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(-\frac{5{x}^{7}}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{10{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{x}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(-5{x}^{4}+\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})}{(10+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{-5{x}^{4}+0}{10+0+0} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{4} \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.

decision.explanation: Dividing by x² gives (x+1/x²)/(2+1/x). As x approaches negative infinity, the denominator approaches 2 and the numerator approaches negative infinity, so the limit is negative infinity.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{{x}^{3}+1}{2{x}^{2}+x} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(\frac{{x}^{3}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{2{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{x}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{(x+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})}{(2+\frac{1}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{(x+0)}{(2+0)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{x}{2} \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: What is the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ for $x>0$ with $f(x)=\frac{|{x}^{3}-5|}{2-{x}^{3}}?$
after.worked_solution:
For large positive values of $x,$ we have $|{x}^{3}-5|=({x}^{3}-5).$ Consequently, for $x\to \infty ,$ we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{|{x}^{3}-5|}{2-{x}^{3}}={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{{x}^{3}-5}{2-{x}^{3}}.
$$

The horizontal asymptote for $x>0$ is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{3}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{{x}^{3}-5}{2-{x}^{3}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{5}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(1-\frac{5}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}-1)} \\  & =\frac{1-0}{0-1} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote is $y=-1.$

after.problem:
What is the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ for $x<0$ with $f(x)=\frac{|8x-7|}{-5x+2}?$

The horizontal asymptote is $y=$

{{field-1}}.
after.worked_solution:
For large negative values of $x,$ we have $|8x-7|=-(8x-7).$ Consequently, for $x\to -\infty ,$ we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{|8x-7|}{-5x+2}={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-(8x-7)}{-5x+2}.
$$

The horizontal asymptote for $x<0$ is $y={lim}_{x\to -\infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-(8x-7)}{-5x+2} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-(\frac{8x}{x}-\frac{7}{x})}{(\frac{-5x}{x}+\frac{2}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-(8-\frac{7}{x})}{(-5+\frac{2}{x})} \\  & =\frac{-(8-0)}{-5+0} \\  & =\frac{8}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote is $y=\frac{8}{5}.$

EXPLANATION

For large negative values of x, we have |8x−7|=−(8x−7). Consequently, for x→−∞, we get

limx→−∞|8x−7|−5x+2=limx→−∞−(8x−7)−5x+2.

The horizontal asymptote for x<0 is y=limx→−∞f(x). To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of x in the denominator, which is x.

limx→−∞f(x)=limx→−∞−(8x−7)−5x+2=limx→−∞−(8xx−7x)(−5xx+2x)=limx→−∞−(8−7x)(−5+2x)=−(8−0)−5+0=85.

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote is y=85.

For large negative values of $x,$ we have $|8x-7|=-(8x-7).$ Consequently, for $x\to -\infty ,$ we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{|8x-7|}{-5x+2}={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-(8x-7)}{-5x+2}.
$$

The horizontal asymptote for $x<0$ is $y={lim}_{x\to -\infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-(8x-7)}{-5x+2} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-(\frac{8x}{x}-\frac{7}{x})}{(\frac{-5x}{x}+\frac{2}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-(8-\frac{7}{x})}{(-5+\frac{2}{x})} \\  & =\frac{-(8-0)}{-5+0} \\  & =\frac{8}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote is $y=\frac{8}{5}.$
